subject: Private VPC: networking scope, PrivateLink vs peering and egress allowlist — next steps
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@finvault.com>, David Lu <dlu@finvault.com>
Cc: secops@finvault.com
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + asks — Private VPC networking scope and next steps

Hi Ayesha / David,

Thanks again for a great discovery call earlier today. Quick written recap and concrete asks so we can scope the Private VPC (applies if you decide Private or Dedicated with VPC peering/privatelink):

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary requirement: no internet-facing egress from model hosts; traffic must go to FinVault VPC via PrivateLink or Peering.
- Security wants static outbound IPs for allowlisting third-party services (logging, metrics, licensing callbacks).
- Possible on-prem connector for legacy services is under consideration — timeline TBD.
- Throughput target: ~100 requests/s peak, burst to 300 for 60s.

Asks / next steps (please reply inline):
1) Confirm preferred connectivity model: PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink / endpoint) or VPC peering? If you have an early preference, note why.
2) Provide list of egress allowlist destinations (hostnames/IPs) or confirm we should provide static IP ranges for you to allowlist on your side.
3) Any requirement for customer-managed NAT/proxy (i.e., must outbound go through your NAT gateway) vs Redwood-provided egress IPs?
4) Expected start date for network test window (30–60 min slot) — we usually run a connectivity smoke test before provisioning.

I've attached a short checklist (redwood-privatelink-checklist.pdf) that calls out the common asks from our side.

Proposed internal owners: Ben (networking/egress IPs) and Marissa (deployment sizing / Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs).

If it's helpful, let's tentatively schedule a 30-min technical alignment next week — I can set options once you confirm preferred connectivity model.

Thanks,

--
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182
From: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@finvault.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: David Lu <dlu@finvault.com>, secops@finvault.com
Date: Fri, 1 Jun 2028 18:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + asks — Private VPC networking scope and next steps

Thanks Logan — and appreciate the clear checklist. Inline below.

On Fri, Jun 1, 2028 at 5:05 PM Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> 1) Confirm preferred connectivity model: PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink / endpoint) or VPC peering? If you have an early preference, note why.

We lean toward PrivateLink initially because it minimizes route-table changes and keeps network controls simpler for our infra team. Peering may be considered later if latencies are an issue.

> 2) Provide list of egress allowlist destinations (hostnames/IPs) or confirm we should provide static IP ranges for you to allowlist on your side.

Security prefers static IP ranges we can put into our firewall allowlist. We do NOT want any dynamic IPs. If you can provide a small set of stable egress IPs (or a documented IP range) that would be ideal.

> 3) Any requirement for customer-managed NAT/proxy (i.e., must outbound go through your NAT gateway) vs Redwood-provided egress IPs?

We'd prefer Redwood provide stable egress IPs for the model hosts; however if a proxy is required for cert pinning with our SIEM, we can explore an outbound proxy in the VPC.

> 4) Expected start date for network test window (30–60 min slot) — we usually run a connectivity smoke test before provisioning.

Can we aim for Tue, Jun 5 in the morning PST? David and secops can join.

Attachments: none from our side right now.

Regards,
Ayesha
Director, Cloud Infrastructure
FinVault
From: secops@finvault.com
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@finvault.com>, David Lu <dlu@finvault.com>
Date: Sat, 2 Jun 2028 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap + asks — Private VPC networking scope and next steps

Hi all,

Security follow-up with constraints and a short checklist from our side: (cc'ing a few infra folks who will own allowlist config)

Constraints:
- All model-host egress must originate from fixed IP addresses owned/contracted by Redwood or traverse our customer-managed NAT. No ephemeral ranges.
- TLS inspection is NOT allowed for model request/response traffic.
- We need to run a handshake test against our internal license verification endpoint (https://licence.finvault.internal) from your egress IPs.

Requests:
- Please provide a CIDR / set of IPs (minimum: 2 IPs for redundancy) and an estimated maintenance window schedule for any potential IP rotation.
- Provide an example curl command and expected headers we should allow (we will whitelist by src IP + host header).

On Tue, Jun 1, 2028 at 6:12 PM Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@finvault.com> wrote:
> We lean toward PrivateLink initially...

Thanks,
FinVault Security (secops@finvault.com)
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 2 Jun 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Recap + asks — Private VPC networking scope and next steps

Marissa / Ben — forwarding FinVault's replies and SecOps constraints. Quick internal assignment and proposed answers so we can respond before Monday: 

-- Action items --
Ben: can you prepare a stable egress proposal (two static IPs + maintenance/rotation policy) and a small CSV with the ranges? Attach the ip-ranges-2028-06-02.csv what you'll send to FinVault. Include the sample curl test and exact headers. Deadline: Mon 9am PST.

Marissa: please draft a short note (1-pager) on tradeoffs between PrivateLink vs VPC peering for this workload (latency, ops, cross-account routing, Dedicated vs Hosted implications) and recommended path for FinVault given their throughput (100 req/s baseline). Also add notes if Dedicated capacity would materially change our egress story. Deadline: Mon 10am PST.

I'll coordinate the Tue Jun 5 smoke test scheduling (Ayesha requested morning PST). If you want me to loop in Solutions Engineering mgr or Delivery, say so.

Thanks,
Logan

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear owners.

On Tue Jun 5, morning PST works — let's do 9:30am PST. Please send a calendar invite.

We prefer PrivateLink for the initial rollout based on our infra notes above. For the smoke test, we'll need the two static IPs and the example curl command ahead of time so our firewall team can provision rules.

I'll await Ben's CSV and Marissa's one-pager. If either of you foresee a blocker for providing static IPs (compliance or procurement constraints), flag it now — security will need to know if we must host outbound through our NAT instead.

Thanks,
Ayesha
